description: I'm a passionate backend developer interested in AI, technology, and solving real-world problems. I have experience with Python, FastAPI, databases, and API development. I'm looking for motivated teammates to build an innovative project together. Frontend developers, UI/UX designers, and people with AI/ML or data analysis skills are especially welcome. summary:
ECHOES is an interactive, browser-based space museum for young explorers aged 10–15. Visitors follow four NASA missions through photo-led story chapters: Apollo 11's laser reflector, the Opportunity rover, the InSight lander and Voyager 1. Each chapter ends with a hands-on experiment. Visitors time a laser pulse to the Moon to work out its distance, sort Martian rocks as evidence of ancient water, and find a marsquake in seismograms to read the planet's interior. Around the chapters are a 3D solar system with real landing sites, a mission timeline from 1969 to 2026, three games (a lunar lander, a probe builder and a quiz) and a journal of discoveries and patches.

We built ECHOES to show that NASA's spacecraft are more than history. They are tools that answered real scientific questions, and children can reason through the same steps themselves. Every page uses NASA imagery and cites its scientific sources.

ECHOES is also built to be open to everyone. It works with no account, comes in 11 languages and includes an accessibility panel with high contrast, larger text, reduced motion and a relaxed game mode. Anyone, anywhere, can explore how these machines changed our understanding of the universe.
details:
What it does. ECHOES is a free interactive web museum about space exploration for learners aged 10–15. Visitors follow four NASA missions: Apollo 11, Opportunity, InSight and Voyager 1. Each story ends with an experiment the visitor solves to make the discovery: measuring the distance to the Moon with a laser pulse, finding evidence of water on Mars, reading a marsquake, and matching spacecraft to their status. There is also a 3D solar system with real landing sites, a mission timeline, three games and a journal of discoveries and patches.

Benefits. Students learn by doing, not just reading. Every fact is traced to a NASA source, and simplified models are labelled. The site works in 10 languages, has a full accessibility panel (high contrast, larger text, reduced motion, relaxed games), runs in any browser, and needs no account. Nothing about the visitor is collected.

Intended impact. We want young people everywhere, not only English speakers, to see science as questions, methods and evidence they can follow themselves, and to see that missions launched decades ago still matter today.

Tools. TypeScript, React, three.js, Vite and CSS; Vitest for testing; GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages for deployment. We used NASA photos, planet maps and mission pages as sources. No special hardware was used.

Creativity. ECHOES is a museum built as a game. The idea of an "echo" links all the stories: a laser pulse returning from the Moon, seismic waves inside Mars, Voyager's signal from interstellar space. The design is inspired by real spacecraft materials.

Factors considered. Scientific accuracy, age-appropriate language, accessibility, performance on ordinary phones, and respect for NASA's media guidelines. The project is independent and not endorsed by NASA. AI tools helped with development, and every scientific claim was checked by hand against NASA sources.
